predecessors.name: Ife Confederation
predecessors.text: the Ife region, 'a small collection of house societies in mid-first millennium BCE' grown to the Ife Confederation

successors.name: Oyo Empire
successors.text: Oyo and Jebba in the north, 'encompassed Owu, Jebba, Tada, and Oyo in the north'

ledger.x: c. 1000: the classical Ife begins. 'A classical period starting from 1000 to 1420 CE' (Ife Empire page); the page gives no founding year for the empire itself, and the Ile-Ife page puts the city's founding 'between the years 1000 BC and 500 BC' with a 900 AD emporium.
14th century: Ife stretches to Owu, Jebba, Tada, Oyo and Ijebu.
ledger.cp: Owu, Jebba, Tada and Ijebu (towns and chiefdoms)

ledger.x: 14th century: Oyo is counted in the Ife empire.

wars.name: Owu war against Ife
wars.outcome: Owu, grown rich on horses and cavalry, 'eventually declared war on Ife, starting a civil war' (Ife Empire page); no year, no outcome, no land.

certainty.note: No frontier is given by any page; the extent is the list of towns 'Owu, Jebba, Tada, and Oyo ... and Ijebu' and the 52,000 km2 infobox figure.
